title: fix(plugin-charts): the scatter's numeric axes honour their spec ChartAxis
body:
Fixes #9675

`Clause-②: no`

## What was dropped

`AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` derives every spec-driven numeric-axis prop in one
helper. The scatter branch never spread it, so five keys the spec declares, the
schema accepts and `normalizeChartSchema` resolves were dropped at render for
that one family: `min` / `max` (domain), `stepSize` (ticks), `logarithmic`
(scale) and `title` (label). Nothing refused and nothing looked broken — the
chart drew confidently, at a scale the author had overridden.

Two further readings taken on the branch, both reported to the dispatcher:

- **The x axis had the same gap, and the card names it.** Scatter is this
  renderer's only family whose x is a numeric MEASURE rather than a category
  band, so it is the only one where those keys mean anything on x. The card's
  Expected says "the scatter's numeric **axes**", so both are repaired.
- **`format` was dropped on the scatter y axis too.** Every other y axis in the
  file passes `yTickFormatter` (which resolves the spec `format`); scatter alone
  passed the raw compact default. One identifier, same element, same defect
  class — repaired here rather than left as a half-state inside an element this
  branch is already rewriting.

## Composition with objectui#7396 — checked before adding a domain, as dispatched

The card carried a collision warning: an explicit padding domain and a
spec-derived domain would be the same recharts prop, and whichever landed
second would shadow the other. objectui#7396 (the scatter's visual edge
clipping) landed first, and **it does not collide** — it deliberately spent
recharts' axis `padding`, which insets the pixel RANGE and leaves the domain
alone. Its own docblock says so and names this card by number.

So the two are live at once: the domain is the author's, and no extreme mark is
half-painted outside the plot box. The test
`keeps objectui#7396's edge margin while honouring a pinned domain` holds that
pair together, with a y floor of 12 (not 0) so it witnesses rather than agreeing
with the auto domain by luck. The two docblocks that described the domain prop
as still free — one in the source, one in objectui#7396's own test — are updated
to say it is now spent and the two compose.

objectui#9681's defect (the ZAxis `range` inert for want of a `dataKey`) is
untouched by this branch, per the SERIAL ruling on the card.

## Evidence

Reverse verification, on the final HEAD, with the mutation proved on disk
(anchor counts before/after, blob hash before/after, restore proved by an empty
`git diff HEAD` rather than by an exit code):

| leg | reading |
|:--|:--|
| new pin file before the repair | **8 failed / 2 passed (10)** |
| new pin file after the repair | **12 passed (12)** |
| repair stripped from the final HEAD (ablation) | **10 failed / 2 passed (12)** |
| restored | blob hash equals the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty |

The two that survive the ablation are the controls: with no spec axis declared
the derivation contributes no prop, so the default scatter render is byte-for-byte
the one objectui#7396 measured in real Chromium. That is also why its pinned
default tick arrays are untouched by this branch.

Measured, all from the repo root (the package-directory form is refused by the
invocation guard):

| run | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-charts/` | exit 0 — 62 files, 560 tests passed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/ packages/plugin-report/` | exit 0 — 136 files, 1320 tests passed |
| `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts build` | exit 0 (after building the dependency closure) |
| `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts type-check` | exit 0 — `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test file is covered |
| `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts lint` | exit 0 — 350 warnings, all the pre-existing `no-explicit-any` baseline |

Gates hand-derived from this repo's own `package.json` and `.github/workflows/`
(the objectstack derivation script refuses to answer for this repo), every exit
code redirected to a file before being read: `check-changeset-presence`,
`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-control-bytes`,
`check-new-cross-file-line-citations`, `check-test-path-roots`,
`check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`,
`check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-unreferenced-sources`,
`check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`,
`check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check-spec-symbol-derivation`,
`check-lint-rule-coverage`, `check-lint-coverage` — all exit 0.
`check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the four changed paths reports NOT
GOVERNED. Remote CI is authoritative and has not been waited on.

## Why a headless DOM can measure this

happy-dom reports `clientWidth` 0, so `ResponsiveContainer` would measure
nothing — which is exactly what the harness mock removes. Handed an explicit
width and height, recharts computes the plot rect, the tick values and every
symbol centre arithmetically, with no DOM measurement in the path. The sibling
objectui#7396 file states the same and checked its numbers against a
real-Chromium run of the same chart.

## Scope

The `logarithmic` pin states an invariant rather than a coordinate: four rows in
geometric progression are equally spaced on a log scale and are not on a linear
one, so no pixel is pinned. On the defect that ratio reads 100; the pin requires
it under 1.05.

Deliberately NOT in this diff, reported to the dispatcher instead: the scatter's
`CartesianGrid` is hard-coded `vertical={false}` rather than taking the
per-axis `showGridLines` the rest of the file derives. Different element,
different prop family, and a separate card.

`Clause-②: no` holds against the real diff: no exported symbol is added and no
new key is read. The derivation the other families already use is now a plain
module function shared by both orientations, and the scatter axes spread it.
The changeset is `minor` and says plainly that this is a user-visible render
change.

## Corpus price, taken because nobody had

Nothing in this repo's authored corpus (`examples/schema-catalog`,
`apps/console`, `content/docs`) declares a scatter with any of these keys on an
axis — there is no authored scatter schema in the catalogue at all. The matcher
is lit: the same search finds ten yAxis-with-spec-keys sites elsewhere in the
tree, and the catalogue does carry three authored chart schemas. A zero
in-repo count does not price the change down, though: these are keys the spec
declares and this renderer accepts, and downstream authors are not in this
tree.
